match.header: Install Desiderio and seed a demo page tree

set.header: Install Desiderio and seed a demo page tree
set.bodytext:
Desiderio is not on Packagist, so add the GitHub repositories first. After the install, enable the Desiderio site sets for your site.

# Desiderio and the Visual Editor enhancements it requires are not on Packagist
composer config repositories.desiderio vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/desiderio.git
composer config repositories.visual-editor-enhancements vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-visual-editor-enhancements.git
composer require webconsulting/desiderio
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup
vendor/bin/typo3 cache:flush

# Optional: a demo page tree with every element below page 1
vendor/bin/typo3 desiderio:styleguide:seed --parent=1

The code and the manual are on GitHub. The Desiderio feature page shows the wizard, the presets and the page module in live screenshots.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
Desiderio needs TYPO3 v14.3.6 or newer on the 14.3 LTS branch, with PHP 8.4 or 8.5. It builds on Content Blocks, the Visual Editor and our Visual Editor Enhancements. It does not install on TYPO3 v13.

Desiderio is free under GPL-2.0-or-later, with no licence key and no locked features. The bundled icon fonts keep their own licences. The code passes PHPStan at level 8, and CI runs on PHP 8.4 and 8.5.

match.header: What you get in one Composer package

set.header: What you get in one Composer package
set.bodytext:
• 244 content elements in 10 groups, each with English and German demo content.
  • 62 Fluid components: 17 atoms, 37 molecules, 4 layouts and 4 organisms.
  • 15 theme presets and five icon libraries, chosen in the site settings.
  • Site sets that restyle the Blog extension, News, Apache Solr and Powermail with the same components.
  • 8 Form Framework forms, ready to place and wired to the elements.
  • A seed command that builds a demo page tree with every element.

For new elements from shadcn registries, read our post on Innesto.

match.header: One setting changes the look of every page

set.header: One setting changes the look of every page
set.bodytext:
Pick one of 15 theme presets in the site settings, or set one per page tree. The 15 are 5 shadcn create presets and 10 house presets. Colours, fonts, corners, control sizes and icons change together. Icons come from five libraries: Lucide, Tabler, HugeIcons, Phosphor and Remix.

Records store field values and semantic icon keys, not colours or CSS classes. A preset switch only swaps design tokens, so the same content renders in the new look. Each preset also ships its own dark token set.

match.header: 244 elements in 10 groups, ready for editors

set.header: 244 elements in 10 groups, ready for editors
set.bodytext:
The content wizard lists 10 Desiderio groups next to the core types. They cover heroes, navigation, content, features, pricing, social proof, team, data, conversion and footers. Each element has its own icon, a description and demo content in English and German.

Every element is a Content Block. In the page module, it shows a preview card with its type, headline and key fields. So editors find content without opening forms.

assets.alternative: TYPO3 page module for Hero & Landing Intros with preview cards listing each hero element's type, headline and fields.
assets.description: Preview cards show each element's type, headline and key fields.

match.header: Relaunches keep rebuilding the same sections

set.header: Relaunches keep rebuilding the same sections
set.bodytext:
You build heroes, pricing tables and footers again for each client. Editors wait for a developer whenever they need a new section. A new brand colour means CSS changes and another deployment. The budget goes into rework instead of content.

Desiderio is a design system for TYPO3 v14 that ships these sections finished. Its look follows shadcn/ui, and Fluid renders every element on the server. There is no JavaScript component runtime.

match.header: Install Innesto and graft your first element

set.header: Install Innesto and graft your first element
set.bodytext:
Composer does not inherit repositories from dependencies, so register all three in your project. Then add the webconsulting/innesto site set to your site.

composer config repositories.desiderio vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/desiderio.git
composer config repositories.visual-editor-enhancements vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-visual-editor-enhancements.git
composer config repositories.innesto vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/innesto.git
composer require webconsulting/innesto:^2.3
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup
vendor/bin/typo3 cache:flush
vendor/bin/typo3 innesto:add magicui/marquee --key partner-marquee

The code is on GitHub, and the manual has the command reference and the finishing checklist. The feature page shows Desiderio and Innesto together. For the design system underneath, read our Desiderio post.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
Innesto needs TYPO3 v14.3.7 or newer, PHP 8.4 or newer and Content Blocks 2.4. It builds on Desiderio 4.3 or newer. CI runs PHP 8.4 and 8.5. There is no React runtime and no frontend build step.

Innesto is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. Preserved upstream sources keep their original licences.

match.header: Every graft follows the presets and dark mode

set.header: Every graft follows the presets and dark mode
set.bodytext:
Each graft composes Desiderio components and paints itself only from Desiderio tokens. So it follows all 15 theme presets and dark mode without knowing they exist.

Three test layers hold every element to that contract. A composition test checks which components a template may use. A package test checks metadata, tables, token-only styling and demo data. Desiderio's Fluid 5 linter checks every template.

assets.alternative: Six Desiderio preset cards in teal, blue, violet, blue, green and orange, each with buttons, badges and font details.
assets.description: Innesto elements take their colours and fonts from these presets.

match.header: 19 finished elements, grouped in the wizard

set.header: 19 finished elements, grouped in the wizard
set.bodytext:
Innesto ships 19 finished elements. They include a marquee, orbiting circles, a terminal and case studies. The other 15 are the complete stats family of blocks.so. The frontend is Fluid, CSS and SVG, and only the area chart needs a small JavaScript renderer.

The elements sit in their own groups of the content wizard, such as Magic UI and Stats. The innesto:seed command fills a page with demo content for each element.

match.header: One command writes the element scaffold

set.header: One command writes the element scaffold
set.bodytext:
Run innesto:add with a registry item and a key. Innesto writes a complete element folder: configuration, a Fluid template, a backend preview, labels and an icon. It converts the registry's CSS to Desiderio's semantic tokens. The upstream source stays in the folder for provenance.

React state and props still have to become editor fields. Innesto writes this finishing pass down as a prompt next to the element. You do it by hand, or with the --ai option and the installed Claude CLI. Four registries have shorthands, and any other needs the URL of the item's JSON.

match.header: Registries ship components TYPO3 cannot run

set.header: Registries ship components TYPO3 cannot run
set.bodytext:
The shadcn/ui registries publish hundreds of finished React components. Examples are shadcn itself, Magic UI, shadcnblocks and blocks.so. TYPO3 cannot run them on its pages.

Innesto grafts them instead. It keeps the visual design and the markup structure, and it drops the React runtime. The result is a Content Block whose fields an editor fills in. Innesto is Italian for a graft.

set.title: Astryx for TYPO3: Meta's design system, no React
set.abstract: Astryx for TYPO3 brings Meta's open-source design system to TYPO3 v14 as 250 content elements and 25 themes. Fluid renders everything on the server.

set.og_title: Astryx for TYPO3: Meta's design system, no React
set.og_description: Meta's Astryx design system for TYPO3 v14: 250 content elements and 25 themes, rendered by Fluid on the server, without React or a build step.

match.header: Install Astryx and run the schema script

set.header: Install Astryx and run the schema script
set.bodytext:
TYPO3's own setup cannot add this many columns to tt_content. So you run the included schema script once, with a dry run first. The script currently expects DDEV.

# astryx-typo3 and the packages it builds on are not on Packagist
composer config repositories.astryx-typo3 vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/astryx-typo3.git
composer config repositories.desiderio vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/desiderio.git
composer config repositories.visual-editor-enhancements vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-visual-editor-enhancements.git
composer require webconsulting/astryx-typo3

# extension:setup cannot add the tt_content columns once the table is this wide:
# dry run first, then --apply (the script expects the DDEV docroot /var/www/html)
ddev exec php vendor/webconsulting/astryx-typo3/Build/Scripts/apply-schema.php
ddev exec php vendor/webconsulting/astryx-typo3/Build/Scripts/apply-schema.php --apply

# Add webconsulting/astryx-typo3 and webconsulting/astryx-typo3-content-elements
# to config/sites/<site>/config.yaml, then seed the showcase:
ddev exec vendor/bin/typo3 astryx-typo3:site:seed --content

The code and the manual are on GitHub. The Astryx feature page shows the themes, dark mode and the page theme field.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
Astryx for TYPO3 needs TYPO3 v14.3.7 or newer, PHP 8.4 or newer and Content Blocks 2.2 or newer. Desiderio runs underneath as the rendering engine, and Composer installs it. The Visual Editor is optional: it adds inline editing and the element picker.

The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. Astryx itself is MIT-licensed by Meta, and the bundled fonts use the SIL Open Font License.

match.header: What you get with Astryx for TYPO3

set.header: What you get with Astryx for TYPO3
set.bodytext:
• 250 content elements in 10 groups, with demo content in two languages.
  • 189 Fluid components, reached through one namespace.
  • 25 themes for a site or a page tree, in light and dark mode.
  • A page shell with header, footer, breadcrumb and error pages, driven by site settings.
  • A contrast gate that checks 1,600 colour pairs against WCAG 2.2 AA and fails the build on a miss.
  • Self-hosted fonts, so nothing loads from Meta or a CDN.

match.header: 25 themes, switched per site or per page

set.header: 25 themes, switched per site or per page
set.bodytext:
Meta's release provides seven of the themes, and 18 more follow the same tokens. Set a theme for the site, or override it for a page and its subpages. The Astryx theme field in the page properties does this, and an empty field inherits.

A theme switch is a repaint. Every value is a custom property, so nothing is rebuilt and no content changes. Colour tokens are light and dark pairs, so the colour scheme and the theme switch independently.

assets.alternative: Six Astryx theme cards: Neutral, Butter, Chocolate, Matcha with handwritten headings, Stone and the dark Gothic theme.
assets.description: Six of the 25 themes render the same markup side by side.

match.header: 250 elements in Desiderio's 10 wizard groups

set.header: 250 elements in Desiderio's 10 wizard groups
set.bodytext:
The 250 content elements sit in the 10 wizard groups that Desiderio uses. So editors read the same group names in both design systems. Each group holds 25 elements. Every element has demo content in English and German and a backend preview.

Behind them are 189 Fluid components in four layers: layout, atom, molecule and organism. They render 159 of upstream's 164 components. The other five are React context providers that output no markup. Native HTML handles menus, dialogs and carousels, and one small script covers the rest.

match.header: Design systems often need a JavaScript stack

set.header: Design systems often need a JavaScript stack
set.bodytext:
Most current design systems ship as React components. Meta's Astryx is one of them, styled with StyleX. Bringing it to TYPO3 the usual way means a Node build and a JavaScript runtime on every page. Every change to the look needs a rebuild.

Astryx for TYPO3 ships the same design system as Fluid components and plain CSS. There is no React, no StyleX and no build step after an editor saves. From upstream it takes the token vocabulary and the seven official themes, pinned to release 0.6.2.

set.title: Visual Editor Enhancements: more editing in place
set.abstract: Visual Editor Enhancements adds an element library with live previews, a popover for layout options and link editing. Everything saves through the Visual Editor.
set.description: Add content with live previews, change layout options in a popover and edit links on the page. An add-on for the Visual Editor of TYPO3 v14.
set.og_title: Visual Editor Enhancements: more editing in place
set.og_description: Add content with live previews, change layout options in a popover and edit links on the page. An add-on for the Visual Editor of TYPO3 v14.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: An element library, a field chooser and link editing for the TYPO3 Visual Editor

featured_image.alternative: TYPO3 Visual Editor with the Add content panel open, showing element cards with rendered previews and keyword chips.

match.header: Install Visual Editor Enhancements

set.header: Install Visual Editor Enhancements
set.bodytext:
# Not on Packagist: add the Git repository first
composer config repositories.visual-editor-enhancements vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-visual-editor-enhancements.git
composer require webconsulting/visual-editor-enhancements
vendor/bin/typo3 cache:flush

The field settings and link buttons appear in the Editor module straight away. The code is on GitHub, with the manual next to it. The feature page shows each feature in a screenshot.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
You need TYPO3 v14.3.7 or newer, PHP 8.4 or newer and Visual Editor 1.10.2 or newer. Each release is checked against a named Visual Editor version, currently 1.10.3. The element library also needs a catalogue provider that lists your elements and renders their previews. Desiderio is one, and the other features work on any Visual Editor site.

The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later and ships through Composer and Git. Its endpoints need a backend login and a request token.

match.header: Switch features off per user or page tree

set.header: Switch features off per user or page tree
set.bodytext:
Every feature is on by default. You can switch each one off per installation, per user or per page tree. Page TSconfig can also hide the language view switch and the autosave toggle in the editor's toolbar.

The panels look like the TYPO3 backend, not like the site below them. They take the backend's theme, colour scheme, font and radius. Dialogs, labels, live regions and focus handling follow WCAG 2.2 AA.

match.header: Layout options and links on the page

set.header: Layout options and links on the page
set.bodytext:
The field chooser is a popover with the record's choice fields: selects, category trees, links, checkboxes and colours. It groups them like the backend form. Open it from the element's action bar or from a button on an editable text. Changes wait in the Visual Editor's pending list until you save.

Hover a button, and a chain icon opens the TYPO3 link browser for its link field. The rich-text toolbar sits in one row above the text. Bold, italic, link and bulleted list stay visible, and the other buttons sit behind 'Show more items'.

assets.alternative: Visual Editor with the Field settings popover open on a hero, showing background and spacing options in tabs.
assets.description: The Field settings popover groups the options in the tabs of the backend form.

match.header: An element library with live previews

set.header: An element library with live previews
set.bodytext:
A round button opens a side panel of content element types. Each card is a rendered preview with keyword chips. Drag a card onto a drop zone, and the element arrives pre-filled from its demo record. So a new section never starts empty.

The search forgives typos. Type testimonal, and the library still finds the testimonial elements, with a 'Did you mean' link. Elements you used recently stay at the top.

assets.alternative: Element library search for the misspelt word testimonal, listing testimonial elements and a Did you mean suggestion.
assets.description: A typo still finds the testimonial elements.

match.header: Editing on the page stops at the text

set.header: Editing on the page stops at the text
set.bodytext:
The TYPO3 Visual Editor lets editors type straight into the page. Adding an element still means a list without previews. Layout options, links and colours live in the backend form. So editors switch screens for every small change.

Visual Editor Enhancements fills these gaps without forking the Visual Editor. Saving, permissions and workspaces stay with the Visual Editor.

set.title: Records List Types: the right view per table
set.abstract: Records List Types shows TYPO3 records as photo cards, dense tables, teasers or your own layouts. Records List Examples adds six ready views.
set.description: Grid, compact, teaser and custom views for the TYPO3 v14 Records module, with filters and drafts in view. Six example views show how to build your own.
set.og_title: Records List Types: the right view per table
set.og_description: Grid, compact, teaser and custom views for the TYPO3 v14 Records module, with filters and drafts in view. Six example views show how to build your own.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Grid, compact, teaser and custom views for the Records module of TYPO3 v14

featured_image.alternative: Records module grid view: news cards with Easter-egg photos, German titles, dates and language flags.

match.header: Install both packages with Composer

set.header: Install both packages with Composer
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.records-list-types vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-records-list-types.git
composer config repositories.records-list-examples vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-records-list-examples.git
composer require webconsulting/records-list-types:^2.0 webconsulting/records-list-examples:^2.0
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup -e records_list_types
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup -e records_list_examples
vendor/bin/typo3 cache:flush

Then open the Records module and pick a view from the View menu. The code is on GitHub: Records List Types and Records List Examples. The feature page shows the views in live screenshots.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
Both packages need TYPO3 v14.3.7 or newer on the v14 line, PHP 8.4 or 8.5 and a Composer installation. Install them in the same release, because they ship together.

Both are open source under GPL-2.0-or-later. Records List Types ships English and German labels, plus French, Spanish and Italian drafts.

match.header: Drafts and permissions work as before

set.header: Drafts and permissions work as before
set.bodytext: Every view reads through the same record pipeline as the core list. Permissions, translations, workspaces and record actions behave as before. In a workspace, each view shows draft rows with state markers. Search and filters also find text that only exists in a draft. The extension only stores each editor's view and filter settings.

match.header: Six example views from TSconfig and Fluid

set.header: Six example views from TSconfig and Fluid
set.bodytext:
Records List Examples adds six ready views: Timeline, Catalogue, Address book, Event list, Gallery and Dashboard. Timeline and Catalogue bring their own Fluid template, partials and CSS. The other four are a TSconfig block each, reusing a built-in template.

So most new views need no PHP and no template of their own. For more, register a view in Page TSconfig with your own Fluid template, or through a PSR-14 event.

assets.alternative: Records module catalogue view: large photo cards with title and teaser for each news record.
assets.description: Catalogue is one of the six example views.

match.header: Grid, compact and teaser beside the list

set.header: Grid, compact and teaser beside the list
set.bodytext:
The List view stays the core table, with your chosen columns and every record action. Grid shows records as photo cards. Compact keeps icon, ID and title fixed while the other columns scroll, with sortable headers. Teaser reads like a news list, with title, date and a two-line excerpt.

Filters cover title, date range, visibility, category and any select field. Views of a single table paginate, and views with several tables show a preview with an Expand table link. Editors can also reorder records by drag and drop, with the mouse or the keyboard.

assets.alternative: Records module compact view: a dense table of news with fixed title column and sortable headers.
assets.description: Compact view keeps long lists on one screen.

match.header: One table does not fit every record

set.header: One table does not fit every record
set.bodytext:
The Records module shows news, contacts and products as the same rows of text. Editors scroll sideways to find the article with the right photo. Hidden records and drafts look almost like every other row.

Records List Types adds views to the module's View menu. Editors pick the view that suits each table, and TYPO3 remembers the choice for their next visit.

set.title: Easy Workspace: publish a page in one click
set.abstract: Easy Workspace adds a publishing dropdown to the TYPO3 toolbar. Editors see the pending changes of the page they are on and publish them in one click.
set.description: Publish TYPO3 v14 workspace changes from the toolbar. See what changed on the page in every language, pick what goes live and publish it in one click.
set.og_title: Easy Workspace: publish a page in one click
set.og_description: Publish TYPO3 v14 workspace changes from the toolbar. See what changed on the page in every language, pick what goes live and publish it in one click.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: A toolbar dropdown lists what is pending on the page you are on, in every language

featured_image.alternative: Easy Workspace dropdown listing five pending changes on the People & Team page with New and Changed badges.

match.header: Install Easy Workspace from GitHub

set.header: Install Easy Workspace from GitHub
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.webcon-easy-workspace vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-webcon-easy-workspace.git
composer require webconsulting/webcon-easy-workspace:^1.10
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup
vendor/bin/typo3 cache:flush

Switch to a workspace and open a page, and the toolbar shows what is pending. The code is on GitHub, and the manual explains the badge and every option. The feature page shows the whole flow in screenshots.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
Easy Workspace needs TYPO3 v14.3.6 or newer on the 14.3 LTS line and PHP 8.4 or 8.5, with the core Workspaces extension. EXT:news and the Visual Editor are optional. TSconfig switches single features off per user or group.

Easy Workspace is open source under GPL-2.0-or-later and is released as tags on GitHub.

match.header: Choose what goes live, keep the rest staged

set.header: Choose what goes live, keep the rest staged
set.bodytext:
Every change starts selected. Untick what is not ready, and the button says exactly how many records go live. Each row can open the editor, show the diff and history, or discard one draft. Publish sends the selection live with its related records, and the rest stays in the workspace.

The list comes from the same core code as the Workspaces module. Publishing and discarding go through the DataHandler. So permissions, stages and history stay as they are. The dropdown is hidden in Live.

assets.alternative: Dropdown with two of five changes selected and a Publish 2 button in the footer.
assets.description: Untick what is not ready, and the button counts what goes live.

match.header: Translations are listed, never left behind

set.header: Translations are listed, never left behind
set.bodytext:
The dropdown knows which language you are looking at. Edited elements of the current view come first. Translations follow in a folded section that opens with one click. They stay selected and publish together with the rest.

When you edit an element, TYPO3 also versions its translations as copies. The dropdown marks such a copy as 'Unchanged', not 'Changed'.

assets.alternative: Dropdown with two German changes in view and three English changes under an Other languages heading.
assets.description: Changes in other languages get their own section and stay selected.

match.header: The badge counts changes on this page only

set.header: The badge counts changes on this page only
set.bodytext: The toolbar icon shows how many changes wait on the page you are on, not in the whole site. It counts the same changes the Workspaces module lists for that page, collection items and file references included. The badge updates when something is saved in any frame or browser tab. The dropdown header also says how many changes wait elsewhere in the workspace.

match.header: Publishing should not need an expert

set.header: Publishing should not need an expert
set.bodytext:
The Workspaces module lists changes for whole page trees, not for the page you are on. Editors hunt for their page and guess which records belong to it. Often they leave publishing to an admin, and changes in other languages get missed.

Easy Workspace adds a Workspace publish dropdown to the backend's top bar. It lists the pending changes of the page or news article you are working on. You review and publish them there, without opening the Workspaces module.

composer require webconsulting/docx-editor:^2.2
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup

Running extension:setup creates two small tables. Then Edit DOCX appears in the file list, and every page gets a Word menu. The code is on GitHub. Read the manual or see the feature page.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
DOCX Editor runs on TYPO3 v14.3 LTS from 14.3.7 on, with PHP 8.4 or 8.5; CI tests both. It needs the PHP extensions dom, libxml and zip, and a current browser with WebAssembly. The editor bundle is committed, so you need no Node.js.

The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. It uses only the Apache-2.0 packages of docx-editor.dev, so you need no docx-editor.dev licence.

match.header: Imports that respect your permissions

set.header: Imports that respect your permissions
set.bodytext:
Documents are read with XML entities refused, network access off and size limits against zip bombs. An import runs through the DataHandler with your permissions, workspace and language. If TYPO3 changed between review and import, nothing is written.

New text is split at headings, page breaks and horizontal lines. Each part becomes the content type it fills best. When two types fit equally well, Jev can choose between them.

match.header: Pages travel to Word and back

set.header: Pages travel to Word and back
set.bodytext:
Every page gets a Word menu. Edit in Word opens the page in the embedded editor. Each content element becomes a framed block, and each field becomes a frame inside it. You can also download the page as a .docx file, edit it in Word or LibreOffice, and upload it again.

Before an import, a review lists each element as new, changed, conflicting or removed. Nothing is written until you confirm. A Word document can also become new pages: one page, a page per Heading 1 or a page per page break. New pages start hidden.

assets.alternative: Review changes before saving dialog listing a changed text element, its field marked changed in Word and an Import button.
assets.description: The review lists every change before anything reaches the page.

match.header: Edit .docx files where they are stored

set.header: Edit .docx files where they are stored
set.bodytext:
Choose Edit DOCX on a file in the file list. The file opens full-page with Word's layout, so pages, headers, tables and images look as they do in Word. Save writes it back to the same file, and Save as makes a copy elsewhere. Tracked changes, comments and content controls survive a save, even when the editor does not show them.

A badge shows how many editors have the document open. If someone saved a newer version, your save stops and offers a reload instead. Printing gives one sheet per page, at the document's own paper size.

assets.alternative: DOCX Editor showing a Word document with a ruler and heading buttons, opened from the TYPO3 file list.
assets.description: Edit DOCX opens the file with Word's layout and saves it back.

match.header: Word files and web pages live apart

set.header: Word files and web pages live apart
set.bodytext:
To fix one line in a Word file, you download it, edit it and upload it again. You hope that nobody changed it in the meantime. Page text travels between Word and TYPO3 by copy and paste, and the formatting breaks.

DOCX Editor brings Word editing into the TYPO3 v14 backend. It uses the free, Apache-2.0 packages of docx-editor.dev.

set.title: Image Workbench: edit images in the file list
set.abstract: Image Workbench opens JPEG, PNG and WebP files in a full-page editor and saves a copy next to the original. New images come from a prompt through nr-llm.
set.description: Crop, adjust, filter and annotate JPEG, PNG and WebP images in the TYPO3 v14 file list, and generate new images from a prompt through nr-llm.
set.og_title: Image Workbench: edit images in the file list
set.og_description: Crop, adjust, filter and annotate JPEG, PNG and WebP images in the TYPO3 v14 file list, and generate new images from a prompt through nr-llm.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Crop, adjust and annotate images in TYPO3 v14, and generate new ones from a prompt

featured_image.alternative: TYPO3 file list with photo thumbnails and an open context menu that offers Edit image for cafe-morning.jpg.

match.header: Install Image Workbench with Composer

set.header: Install Image Workbench with Composer
set.bodytext:
# Not on Packagist: add the Git repository first
composer config repositories.image-workbench vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-image-workbench.git
composer require webconsulting/image-workbench
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup

For AI images, store the provider key in nr-llm and set up an image configuration. The code is on GitHub, and the manual lists every TSconfig option. The feature page shows the editor and the save dialog.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
Image Workbench needs TYPO3 v14.3 LTS and PHP 8.4 or newer with the GD extension. AI generation uses nr-llm 0.34 or 0.35. There are no database tables and no site set.

The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later, and the bundled Filerobot Image Editor is open source. Generated images cost what your provider charges, and nr-llm books the spend per user.

match.header: New images from a prompt through nr-llm

set.header: New images from a prompt through nr-llm
set.bodytext:
A side panel takes a description and a size that the configured model supports. The new image arrives as a PNG in the same folder, and generation never overwrites a file.

The prompt goes through nr-llm, which holds the API key, the model and each user's budget. It books each image to the user who made it. Only the prompt leaves the server, and the photo you edit is never sent.

assets.alternative: Generate with AI panel with a prompt about a café counter, a size menu set to landscape and a Generate image button.
assets.description: Describe the image, pick a size and get a new PNG.

match.header: The original stays safe

set.header: The original stays safe
set.bodytext: Save as copy is the default. It asks for a name and writes a new file next to the original. An existing file is never replaced; a number is added instead. Overwrite original asks for confirmation first and then refreshes every thumbnail and crop of the image. Every read and write goes through TYPO3's file permissions.

match.header: Crop, adjust, filter, annotate and resize

set.header: Crop, adjust, filter, annotate and resize
set.bodytext: Pick Edit image among the actions of an image row or from its context menu. Tabs to adjust, fine-tune, filter, annotate and resize sit beside the photo. Crop presets such as 16:9 or 1:1 come from TSconfig, so each backend group can have its own. The editor follows the backend language and the light or dark colour scheme.

assets.alternative: Image Workbench editing a café photo with the Filters tab open and Save as copy and Overwrite original buttons.
assets.description: The original stays untouched until you save.

match.header: Cropping an image means leaving TYPO3

set.header: Cropping an image means leaving TYPO3
set.bodytext:
Editors download the image, open a desktop tool, crop it and upload it again. The old file may still be in use, and nobody knows which version is current. A new visual means waiting for a designer.

Image Workbench puts a full-page image editor into the TYPO3 v14 file list. It works on JPEG, PNG and WebP files and runs entirely in the browser. It builds on interaction ideas from Georg Ringer's image-editor.

set.title: WorkOS Auth: single sign-on for site and backend
set.abstract: WorkOS Auth adds WorkOS sign-in to the TYPO3 frontend and backend. Customers use their company identity, manage their account and invite their team themselves.
set.description: Add WorkOS sign-in to TYPO3 v14: passwords, email codes, social login and SSO for site and backend, with self-service accounts and team invites.
set.og_title: WorkOS Auth: single sign-on for site and backend
set.og_description: Add WorkOS sign-in to TYPO3 v14: passwords, email codes, social login and SSO for site and backend, with self-service accounts and team invites.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Passwords, email codes, social login and SSO for the TYPO3 frontend and backend

featured_image.alternative: WorkOS sign-in card on the website with email, password, email code and Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Apple.

match.header: Install and run the Setup Assistant

set.header: Install and run the Setup Assistant
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.workos-auth vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/workos.git
composer require webconsulting/workos-auth
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup --extension=workos_auth

Enter the API key and Client ID in the Setup Assistant, and copy the listed redirect URIs into the WorkOS dashboard. Then place the WorkOS Login element on a page. The code is on GitHub, and the feature page shows each screen.

match.header: What it needs and what it costs

set.header: What it needs and what it costs
set.bodytext:
WorkOS Auth needs TYPO3 v14.3.7 or newer and PHP 8.4. Composer installs the WorkOS PHP SDK 9.4. You also need a WorkOS account with AuthKit enabled.

The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. WorkOS bills its own service separately, according to its current plans.

match.header: Security and where user data lives

set.header: Security and where user data lives
set.bodytext:
• PKCE with a client secret, and single-use state bound to a cookie.
  • Redirects stay on your own site.
  • The API key is write-only in the backend, and there are no impersonated backend sessions.
  • Profiles stay in WorkOS. TYPO3 keeps a table that links each WorkOS identity to a frontend or backend user.
  • An account is matched by email only when WorkOS has verified the address.

match.header: The same identity in the TYPO3 backend

set.header: The same identity in the TYPO3 backend
set.bodytext:
Editors pick Login with WorkOS on the backend login screen, and the classic username form stays one click away. The backend also gets a WorkOS menu with a Setup Assistant and a User Management module. The Setup Assistant lists every redirect URI to register in WorkOS, each with its own copy button.

The extension also runs a TYPO3 MCP server behind WorkOS. It accepts anonymous calls in the Development context and needs AuthKit bearer tokens in Production.

assets.alternative: TYPO3 backend login card with WorkOS email sign-in, email code, social buttons and SSO or passkey option.
assets.description: The backend login offers WorkOS sign-in next to the classic form.

match.header: Sign-in screens you do not have to build

set.header: Sign-in screens you do not have to build
set.bodytext:
Three frontend plugins cover the customer side. WorkOS Login handles passwords, email codes, social sign-in, sign-up and email verification. Account Center lets people manage their profile, password, TOTP and sessions. Team lets organisation admins invite colleagues and open Admin Portal links for SSO, Directory Sync and audit logs.

Social sign-in covers Google, Microsoft, GitHub and Apple. You switch sign-in methods on in the WorkOS dashboard, not in TYPO3.

assets.alternative: WorkOS 'Create your account' form with name, email, password and confirmation fields.
assets.description: New customers create an account on your site.

match.header: Every login you build is another project

set.header: Every login you build is another project
set.bodytext:
Customers expect to sign in with the identity their company already uses. Building SSO, MFA, email codes and team invitations yourself takes months. The backend then needs the same work again.

WorkOS Auth connects TYPO3 v14 to WorkOS AuthKit. The same WorkOS account signs people in to your website and to the TYPO3 backend. TYPO3 still creates its own session, and logging out of TYPO3 ends the WorkOS session.

set.title: x402 Paywall: sell pages to people and agents
set.abstract: x402 Paywall sells TYPO3 pages and API routes for small USDC amounts. Browsers get a wallet paywall, and AI agents pay through HTTP headers.
set.description: Sell TYPO3 v14 pages and API routes with HTTP 402. People pay from a browser wallet, AI agents pay in headers, and USDC settles in the same request.
set.og_title: x402 Paywall: sell pages to people and agents
set.og_description: Sell TYPO3 v14 pages and API routes with HTTP 402. People pay from a browser wallet, AI agents pay in headers, and USDC settles in the same request.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: HTTP 402 payments in USDC for TYPO3 pages and API routes, with no accounts

featured_image.alternative: x402 payment page: 'Payment required', price 0.01 USDC on Base Sepolia and a Pay button.

match.header: Install x402 Paywall and start on a testnet

set.header: Install x402 Paywall and start on a testnet
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.x402-paywall vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-x402-paywall.git
composer require webconsulting/typo3-x402-paywall
vendor/bin/typo3 database:updateschema

Add a wallet address to your site configuration, tick one page and run the simulator. Start on Base Sepolia before real money moves. The code is on GitHub, and the manual covers every setting. The feature page shows the flow.

match.header: What it needs and what it stores

set.header: What it needs and what it stores
set.bodytext:
You need TYPO3 v14.3 LTS or later in Composer mode, PHP 8.4 or newer and outbound HTTPS to a facilitator. The x402.org facilitator serves testnets. For mainnet, use a mainnet facilitator such as Coinbase CDP with its API key. Payments work on Base, Base Sepolia, Polygon, Arbitrum, Ethereum or any eip155 chain, with USDC by default.

Each settlement attempt is logged with page, amount, network, payer wallet, transaction hash, status and user agent. The IP address is stored only as a keyed hash. The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later.

match.header: A dashboard, a simulator and MCP tools

set.header: A dashboard, a simulator and MCP tools
set.bodytext:
The backend module shows settled revenue, settlement states and a configuration check per site. A simulator plays the client side: it requests a paid page and decodes the HTTP 402 answer. So you can test the flow without spending money.

Agents get MCP tools too, such as x402_probe and x402_stats, when the MCP Server is installed.

assets.alternative: x402 Paywall dashboard with revenue cards, a site configuration table and recent settlement attempts.
assets.description: Revenue, settlement states and a configuration check for each site.

match.header: Prices per page and per API route

set.header: Prices per page and per API route
set.bodytext: Editors tick Sell this page with x402 in the page properties. They can set a price and a prompt text for people and agents. Route patterns in the site configuration put whole API sections behind the paywall, and free routes always win.

assets.alternative: TYPO3 page properties tab 'x402 Paywall' with the sell toggle, price and payment prompt fields.
assets.description: The paywall is switched on per page, with an optional price.

match.header: A paywall page for people, headers for agents

set.header: A paywall page for people, headers for agents
set.bodytext:
Browsers get a payment page. It connects MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Rabby or another EIP-1193 wallet, then loads the content. API clients and AI agents get HTTP 402 with the terms in a header. They sign a USDC authorisation and retry, with no account, session or card form.

The extension implements version 2 of the x402 HTTP transport. An optional mode also accepts clients that still speak version 1.

match.header: Small payments cost more than they earn

set.header: Small payments cost more than they earn
set.bodytext:
Selling one article or one API call means accounts, card forms and fees that eat small amounts. AI agents cannot fill in a checkout at all, so paid content stays out of their reach.

x402 Paywall uses the x402 HTTP payment protocol instead. A paid page answers 402 Payment Required. The client pays in USDC with a signed authorisation, and a facilitator verifies and settles it on-chain. The content arrives in the same request.

set.title: AI Assistant: a backend chat that asks first
set.abstract: AI Assistant is a chat in the TYPO3 backend that answers questions about your installation with its own tools. Every change waits for your approval.
set.description: A chat in the TYPO3 v14 backend that answers questions about your site with its own MCP tools and asks before it changes anything.
set.og_title: AI Assistant: a backend chat that asks first
set.og_description: A chat in the TYPO3 v14 backend that answers questions about your site with its own MCP tools and asks before it changes anything.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Ask about your TYPO3 installation, and approve every change before it is written

featured_image.alternative: AI Assistant module: conversation list, empty chat with suggested questions, and details with model, tools and limits.

match.header: Install AI Assistant with Composer

set.header: Install AI Assistant with Composer
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.typo3-mcp-server vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-mcp-server.git
composer config repositories.typo3-abilities vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-abilities.git
composer config repositories.typo3-ai-assistant vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-ai-assistant.git
composer require webconsulting/typo3-ai-assistant:^2.0
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup
# Needs one working nr-llm configuration (default identifier: backend-assistant).
# Then open Administration > AI Assistant > Chat.

The MCP Server fork needs the repository of the Abilities Registry too. Give editors access to the AI Assistant module, and they can start asking. The code is on GitHub, and the feature page shows a full conversation.

match.header: What it needs and where your data goes

set.header: What it needs and where your data goes
set.bodytext:
You need TYPO3 v14.3 on PHP 8.4, nr-llm 0.35 with one working configuration and the MCP Server fork 0.9. The tools run inside TYPO3 as the signed-in user. Your question, the tool results and any attachment text go to the provider of your nr-llm configuration. API keys stay encrypted in nr-vault.

The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. You pay your AI provider for the tokens each turn uses, and nr-llm shows usage and estimated cost. By default, each user may start 60 turns an hour.

match.header: The chat follows you through the backend

set.header: The chat follows you through the backend
set.bodytext: The toolbar dropdown keeps the conversation open across modules. It sends the page and workspace you are on with each message. The Chat module shows your conversations with their changes, tool calls, usage and limits. Administrators write instruction records that go into every conversation's system prompt.

match.header: Every write stops and waits for you

set.header: Every write stops and waits for you
set.bodytext:
A write pauses the turn and shows a card with the tool and its arguments. Approve, and it runs; deny, and nothing changes. Write tools stay off until an administrator enables them in nr-llm. User TSconfig can remove tools per backend group, but it can never add any.

Every record the assistant wrote is listed with the conversation, one click from the record editor. In our lab, an approved change lands as a draft in the Staging workspace.

assets.alternative: Approval card for a WriteTable call with its JSON arguments, Deny and Approve buttons, and a waiting notice in the details.
assets.description: Nothing is written until you approve the call.

match.header: Answers come from the site's own tools

set.header: Answers come from the site's own tools
set.bodytext: The assistant calls the tools of the MCP Server in process, as the signed-in backend user. There is no HTTP self-call and no tool server to register. It reads page trees, records, redirects and the system log. Each answer shows the tool calls it made and their results, then explains them in plain words.

assets.alternative: Chat with a question about the Features page tree, three read-only tool calls and the answer that lists every feature page.
assets.description: Three read-only tool calls, then an answer in plain words.

match.header: Answers hide behind too many clicks

set.header: Answers hide behind too many clicks
set.bodytext:
Say you want to know which pages sit below Features, or what the log recorded last night. Finding out means clicking through page trees, lists and logs. Most AI tools that could help want broad access to your site.

AI Assistant is a chat inside the TYPO3 v14 backend. It reads pages and records with the permissions of the signed-in user. When it wants to change something, it stops and asks.

set.title: Jev: forms that read before they route
set.abstract: Jev brings TypeSafe AI's typed decisions into TYPO3 v14. Powermail forms then show the fields that apply and send each message to the right team.
set.description: Jev reads what visitors type into TYPO3 Powermail forms, shows only the fields that apply and routes each message to the right team.
set.og_title: Jev: forms that read before they route
set.og_description: Jev reads what visitors type into TYPO3 Powermail forms, shows only the fields that apply and routes each message to the right team.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Typed AI decisions in TYPO3 Powermail forms: the right fields and the right team

featured_image.alternative: Support form where a described bug revealed the extra field 'How can we reproduce it?'.

match.header: Install Jev and store your TypeSafe key

set.header: Install Jev and store your TypeSafe key
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.webcon-jev vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-webcon-jev.git
composer require webconsulting/webcon-jev
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup
# Put your TypeSafe key into TYPESAFE_API_KEY, then move it into nr-vault:
vendor/bin/typo3 webcon-jev:token:import
vendor/bin/typo3 webcon-jev:ping

Try a decision in the playground before any form uses it. The code and the manual are on GitHub. The feature page shows the forms at work, and DOCX Editor uses Jev as well.

match.header: What it needs and where data goes

set.header: What it needs and where data goes
set.bodytext:
Jev needs TYPO3 v14.3 LTS and PHP 8.4 or newer, with nr-vault for the API token. The Powermail features need the TYPO3 v14 forks of powermail and powermail_cond. The values a decision reads go to the Jev API of TypeSafe. The token stays on the server and never reaches a browser.

The extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. Jev is a managed API, so you need a key from TypeSafe. In our lab, 133 calls cost about 0.002 US cents each on average. Without a token, during an outage or with an unsure answer, the form keeps working with the decision's default.

match.header: Mail reaches the right team

set.header: Mail reaches the right team
set.bodytext: A Powermail form gains a Jev routing tab. Pick a decision and the question that names the receiver. The decision runs when the submission is saved, and its answer picks the address. Below the confidence threshold, the form's own receiver gets the mail. What Jev decided, and how sure it was, is written onto the mail record.

assets.alternative: Powermail form record in TYPO3 with the Jev routing tab: decision and deciding question selected.
assets.description: The routing tab lets a decision choose the receiver.

match.header: Fields that follow the message

set.header: Fields that follow the message
set.bodytext:
With the TYPO3 v14 fork of powermail_cond, a rule gains six Jev operators, such as Jev chose and scored at least. A support form can then ask for reproduction steps only when a message reports a bug. Several rules that read one decision cost one call per request.

A quality gate uses the same rules. A message with nothing to answer hides the send button and shows a note. Borderline messages go through, because a false alarm costs a lead.

match.header: Decisions editors write and test first

set.header: Decisions editors write and test first
set.bodytext:
A decision is a named set of questions about one kind of state. It has a confidence threshold and a default for unsure answers. Decisions are ordinary TYPO3 records, so they can be translated and keep a history.

The backend module has a playground that runs a decision on sample text before any form uses it. The run log records each call with its answers, latency, tokens and cost. The module also counts fallbacks per decision, so a silent failure shows up.

assets.alternative: Jev playground result: a support message classified as a bug with confidence and severity distribution.
assets.description: The playground shows each answer with its confidence and distribution.

match.header: Forms react to clicks, not to meaning

set.header: Forms react to clicks, not to meaning
set.bodytext:
A form reacts to what someone clicks or types, not to what they mean. Every message lands in one inbox, and a person forwards it to sales, support or accounting. Meanwhile, visitors answer questions that do not apply to them.

Jev is the System One model of TypeSafe AI, and it does not generate text. It answers typed questions about a state with a choice, a score or a probability, each with a confidence. Its speed and price make it usable inside a form, while someone is still typing.

set.title: Skillflow: the same AI review for every draft
set.abstract: Skillflow runs agent skills on TYPO3 pages and workspace stages and keeps every report. Your skill library becomes a searchable catalogue with a page per skill.
set.description: Run agent skills on TYPO3 v14 pages and workspace stages, keep every report and publish your skill library as a searchable Solr catalogue.
set.og_title: Skillflow: the same AI review for every draft
set.og_description: Run agent skills on TYPO3 v14 pages and workspace stages, keep every report and publish your skill library as a searchable Solr catalogue.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Run agent skills on pages and workspace stages, and keep every report

featured_image.alternative: Skill catalogue on a TYPO3 page: a search for security with 24 results and facet filters for source, tools and licence.

match.header: Install Skillflow from GitHub

set.header: Install Skillflow from GitHub
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.skillflow vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/skillflow.git
composer require webconsulting/skillflow:^1.9
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup
vendor/bin/typo3 cache:flush
# Catalogue: add the site set webconsulting/skillflow-solr to your site

Then add a skill source in nr-llm and assign your first skill to a workspace stage. The code is on GitHub, and the manual lists every command. The feature page shows the catalogue and a report.

match.header: What it needs and where content goes

set.header: What it needs and where content goes
set.bodytext:
Skillflow needs TYPO3 v14.3.7 or later with PHP 8.4, nr-llm 0.34 or 0.35 and EXT:solr 14.0.1 for the catalogue. Content leaves the server only when a skill runs: the page goes to the model provider you configured. By default, skills run only in a local DDEV installation in the Development context.

Skills can declare the abilities they need, and skillflow:skills:check reports missing or denied ones. With the Claude Code runner, a skill may use only the tools and abilities it declares. Skillflow is free under GPL-2.0-or-later, like TYPO3.

match.header: A catalogue visitors can search

set.header: A catalogue visitors can search
set.bodytext: Publish your active skills with Solr search and translated facets. Each skill gets a detail page with its skill ID, licence, version and allowed tools. The detail element also sets the page title and meta description. Imported skills keep their own licences, and the catalogue shows them.

assets.alternative: Detail page of the security-audit skill with its description, a copyable skill ID, licence, version and allowed tools.
assets.description: Each skill gets its own page with ID, licence and allowed tools.

match.header: Reviews that start with your workflow

set.header: Reviews that start with your workflow
set.bodytext:
Assign skills in the Skills tab of pages, backend users or custom workspace stages. On a stage, switch on auto-run, and every record sent to that stage gets reviewed. You can also run skills in the Skills module on the selected page, or from the CLI.

Each run keeps its status, verdict, engine and a Markdown report. Reports are advice, and Skillflow applies nothing by itself.

assets.alternative: Workspace stage form in TYPO3 with three assigned skills and the switch that runs them on every stage change.
assets.description: Skills on a custom workspace stage, with auto-run switched on.

match.header: Skills from git, reviewed before they run

set.header: Skills from git, reviewed before they run
set.bodytext:
Sync SKILL.md files from a git repository. New skills arrive switched off. A changed skill is switched off again until someone reviews it. Hidden, disabled and orphaned skills never run.

To check skills for risky instructions before you switch them on, see Skillspector.

match.header: Every reviewer checks something different

set.header: Every reviewer checks something different
set.bodytext:
SEO, accessibility and tone rules often live in one person's head or an old wiki page. Drafts get whatever check the reviewer remembers that day. Prompts pasted into a chat window leave no record of what was checked.

Skillflow runs agent skills inside TYPO3 v14. A skill is a SKILL.md file with instructions for an AI model. nr-llm manages the skill sources, imports and activation. Skillflow stores where each skill applies, runs it and keeps the report.

set.title: Skillspector: security checks for agent skills
set.abstract: Skillspector reads every agent skill before your AI does. It flags prompt injection, secrets, risky commands and licence problems, and an administrator decides what to hide.
set.description: Check agent skills for prompt injection, secrets, risky commands and licence problems before your AI follows them, with advisory checks in TYPO3 v14.
set.og_title: Skillspector: security checks for agent skills
set.og_description: Check agent skills for prompt injection, secrets, risky commands and licence problems before your AI follows them, with advisory checks in TYPO3 v14.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Find prompt injection, secrets, risky commands and licence problems before your AI does

featured_image.alternative: Skills Inspector module in TYPO3 listing 60 skills with review-level filters, licence badges and SkillSpector results.

match.header: Install Skillspector next to nr-llm

set.header: Install Skillspector next to nr-llm
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.skillspector vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-skillspector.git
composer require webconsulting/skillspector:^1.2
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup --extension=skillspector
# Optional: the NVIDIA scanner
uv tool install git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git

To run the skills you trust on your pages, read our Skillflow post. The code is on GitHub, and the manual describes every check. The feature page shows the module.

match.header: What it needs and what leaves the server

set.header: What it needs and what leaves the server
set.bodytext:
Skillspector needs TYPO3 v14.3 with PHP 8.4 and nr-llm 0.34 or 0.35, which stores the skills. The scheduler and the NVIDIA scanner are optional. The built-in checks run locally and never fetch or run referenced scripts. Only the optional semantic analysis sends skill content to nr-llm's default provider, and it is off by default.

Skillspector is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. NVIDIA SkillSpector is a separate program that you install yourself.

match.header: An administrator decides, never the check

set.header: An administrator decides, never the check
set.bodytext:
Checks never enable, disable or hide a skill. An administrator reads the evidence and hides a skill only after a confirmation. Its enabled state in nr-llm stays as it is.

The skillspector:check command runs the same scan from cron or the scheduler. It refreshes every report and can email action messages to the addresses you set.

assets.alternative: Confirmation dialog in TYPO3 asking whether to hide the php-modernization skill, with Cancel and Hide buttons.
assets.description: Hiding a skill always needs a confirmation.

match.header: Findings with evidence, not just a warning

set.header: Findings with evidence, not just a warning
set.bodytext: Open the Skills Inspector module and click Check all skills. Filter by review level and read the evidence per skill. Each finding shows its severity, location, the matched text and what to check. Built-in findings and SkillSpector results sit side by side. The module is in English and German and follows the backend's light and dark mode.

assets.alternative: Findings for the php-modernization skill: a destructive rm -rf command, an autonomy prompt and three SkillSpector warnings.
assets.description: Each finding names its severity, location and matched text.

match.header: Three checks over every skill

set.header: Three checks over every skill
set.bodytext:
The checks run over the stored SKILL.md text, its front matter and its code examples.

  • Security scan: 15 built-in rules find prompt injection, exposed keys, pipe-to-shell, fork bombs, exfiltration endpoints and destructive commands.
  • Licence check: when a skill ships code, its declared licence is compared with GPL-2.0-or-later.
  • NVIDIA SkillSpector: if its binary is installed, its findings and risk score join the report.

A missing NVIDIA binary is reported as unavailable, and the built-in checks still run.

match.header: Skills are instructions from strangers

set.header: Skills are instructions from strangers
set.bodytext:
A skill is text your AI agent will follow, often copied from a public repository. One hidden line can leak a key, pipe a script into a shell or skip confirmations. Nobody reads every line before switching a skill on.

Skillspector reads the skills that nr-llm manages before the model does. It tells a person what it found, with evidence.

set.title: Abilities Registry: one rulebook for AI agents
set.abstract: The Abilities Registry lists what your TYPO3 installation can do, with scopes, risk tiers and a site-wide policy. Every surface runs it the same way and logs each attempt.
set.description: One typed registry of what your TYPO3 v14 site can do. MCP, CLI, REST and the backend run each ability under one policy, with scopes and a trace log.
set.og_title: Abilities Registry: one rulebook for AI agents
set.og_description: One typed registry of what your TYPO3 v14 site can do. MCP, CLI, REST and the backend run each ability under one policy, with scopes and a trace log.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: Describe an action once, and MCP, CLI, REST and the backend run it under one policy

featured_image.alternative: Abilities registry with 13 abilities, risk badges from low to critical, scopes, side effects, surfaces and Run buttons.

match.header: Install the Abilities Registry

set.header: Install the Abilities Registry
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.typo3-abilities vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-abilities.git
composer require webconsulting/typo3-abilities:^1.3
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup --extension=abilities
vendor/bin/typo3 abilities:list

The code and the manual are on GitHub. The feature page shows the catalogue and the traces. Our llms.txt extension lists your abilities for agents.

match.header: What it needs and how it compares

set.header: What it needs and how it compares
set.bodytext:
The registry needs TYPO3 v14.3 on PHP 8.4 or 8.5, installed with Composer from GitHub. The MCP Server, EXT:reactions, workspaces and skill extensions are optional, and each adds a surface when present. Webhooks use the Run ability reaction type, and read-only abilities also feed Fluid templates through a data processor.

The registry follows the vocabulary and REST layout of the WordPress Abilities API from core 6.9. It adds scopes, risk tiers, side effects and a site-wide policy. The licence is GPL-2.0-or-later.

match.header: A trace for every attempt, denials included

set.header: A trace for every attempt, denials included
set.bodytext:
Each run records the ability, surface, input, outcome, duration and backend user id. Denied attempts stay in the log for audits. Traces are pruned after 30 days by default. REST tokens are saved as SHA-256 hashes, and the plaintext is shown once.

A catalogue lists everything an agent could use: abilities, MCP tools, skills, REST endpoints and console commands. Each entry says how to call it on every surface.

assets.alternative: Traces table, newest first, with ok and failed runs from MCP and CLI, durations, backend user ids and JSON inputs.
assets.description: Allowed, denied and failed runs all land in the trace log.

match.header: People approve the risky actions

set.header: People approve the risky actions
set.bodytext:
A policy file marks high-risk abilities as review required. They run only after a person approves them, with the --approve-review flag on the CLI or the checkbox in the backend module. REST, MCP and webhook calls cannot approve, and REST answers 409. A risk cap can stop critical abilities from running at all.

Scopes for editors are granted per backend group, and administrators hold every scope.

assets.alternative: Run tab with the Delete page ability selected, its input form, the Approve review checkbox and the Execute button.
assets.description: A person ticks Approve review before a high-risk ability runs.

match.header: An ability is one PHP class

set.header: An ability is one PHP class
set.bodytext:
An ability is a PHP class with one #[AsAbility] attribute. The attribute holds its name, scopes, risk tier and side effects. JSON Schemas describe the input and the output.

Every call walks one pipeline: policy gate, input check, scope check, permission check, execution and output check. Eight abilities ship with the extension, for example content/search and workspace/publish.

match.header: Each protocol brings its own checks

set.header: Each protocol brings its own checks
set.bodytext:
MCP, REST, webhooks and the CLI each get their own endpoints and their own checks. The rules drift apart, and nobody can say which agent did what. An audit then turns into guesswork.

The Abilities Registry describes each action once. MCP, the CLI, REST, webhooks, Fluid and the backend module then run it through the same checks.

set.title: Agent Nexus: try five agent protocols on TYPO3
set.abstract: Agent Nexus runs five agent protocols on your TYPO3 site, with endpoints, live demos and a traffic log. Every write waits for a person, and every payment is simulated.
set.description: Run A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP and AP2 on your own TYPO3 v14 site. You get public endpoints, live demos, a traffic log and approval before every write.
set.og_title: Agent Nexus: try five agent protocols on TYPO3
set.og_description: Run A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP and AP2 on your own TYPO3 v14 site. You get public endpoints, live demos, a traffic log and approval before every write.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP and AP2 with public endpoints, live demos and a traffic log

featured_image.alternative: Protocol hub on a TYPO3 page with cards for A2UI, AG-UI and A2A, their endpoints, spec versions and ready status.

match.header: Install Agent Nexus and seed the demo site

set.header: Install Agent Nexus and seed the demo site
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.agent-nexus vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-agent-nexus.git
composer require webconsulting/agent-nexus:^4.0
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup
vendor/bin/typo3 cache:flush
# Optional: build the demo site
vendor/bin/typo3 agentnexus:seed-site --base=https://example.com/

Schedule agentnexus:cleanup daily so the retention settings apply. The code and the manual are on GitHub, and the feature page shows the demos.

match.header: What it needs, with or without a model

set.header: What it needs, with or without a model
set.bodytext:
Agent Nexus needs TYPO3 v14.3.7 or later and PHP 8.4 with ext-openssl, plus fluid_styled_content. You do not need a language model. Without nr-llm, every protocol runs a deterministic script, the same one the tests check. With nr-llm, you switch the model on per protocol and set a daily budget.

Agent Nexus is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. The official specification schemas used by its tests keep their own licences, Apache-2.0 and MIT.

match.header: A person approves every write

set.header: A person approves every write
set.bodytext:
AG-UI stops for approval before anything is sent. UCP completes a checkout only after the visitor agrees, and AP2 verifies signed mandates. Payments are always simulated. Keep the two 'really apply' switches off, and approved writes and checkouts stay simulated as well.

The traffic log keeps each request, response and streamed event. Names, email addresses, phone numbers and postal addresses are masked before they are stored.

assets.alternative: Agent Nexus traffic log in TYPO3 with the latest A2UI, AG-UI and UCP requests, status codes, durations and event counts.
assets.description: Every request, response and event is on record.

match.header: Demos editors can place on a page

set.header: Demos editors can place on a page
set.bodytext: Each protocol has public endpoints, a backend console that shows the raw traffic and a content element with its live demo. In the A2UI demo, one sentence becomes a working form. TYPO3 draws only components from its trusted catalogue and drops everything else. In the AG-UI demo, the run arrives as a stream of typed events and stops for your approval.

assets.alternative: A2UI demo on a TYPO3 page with the request for a project quote and the form the agent generated from it.
assets.description: One sentence in, a working form out.

match.header: Five protocols and the question each answers

set.header: Five protocols and the question each answers
set.bodytext:
• A2UI: how an agent puts a form on a page without shipping code.
  • AG-UI: how a person watches an agent work and approves before it writes.
  • A2A: how another agent discovers this one and delegates a task.
  • UCP: how a shopping agent checks out with a merchant.
  • AP2: how you prove that a specific person approved a specific purchase.

The versions are A2A 1.0, AG-UI 1.0, A2UI v0.9.1, UCP 2026-08-25 and AP2 v0.2.0. Every payload is tested against the official JSON Schema of its specification.

match.header: Agent protocols are hard to judge from slides

set.header: Agent protocols are hard to judge from slides
set.bodytext:
Clients ask what A2A, AG-UI or UCP would mean for their site. The specifications keep moving, and a slide cannot show a real request or an approval step. You need something that runs on TYPO3 and that you can inspect.

Agent Nexus runs five agent protocols against your own TYPO3, at their current specification versions.

set.abstract: Backend users click an element in the TYPO3 frontend or backend and write a note. Claude Code, Cursor or another MCP agent gets it with selector and styles.
set.description: Click an element on a TYPO3 v14 page or backend screen and write a note. Your coding agent gets it over MCP with selector, page and computed styles.
set.og_title: Agentation: page feedback for coding agents
set.og_description: Click an element on a TYPO3 v14 page or backend screen and write a note. Your coding agent gets it over MCP with selector, page and computed styles.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team

featured_image.alternative: The home page with the Agentation toolbar, two numbered notes on the headline and main button, and a third note in progress.

match.header: Install Agentation and connect your agent

set.header: Install Agentation and connect your agent
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.agentation vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-agentation.git
composer require webconsulting/agentation:^1.5
# Register the MCP server with your coding agent, for example Claude Code:
claude mcp add agentation -- npx -y agentation-mcp server

Then switch the toolbar on in User Settings. The code is on GitHub. Read the manual or see the feature page.

match.header: What it needs and how it is licensed

set.header: What it needs and how it is licensed
set.bodytext:
Agentation needs TYPO3 v14.3 with the Admin Panel and PHP 8.4. The toolbar bundle is built and committed, so your installation needs no Node.js.

The TYPO3 extension is free under GPL-2.0-or-later. It bundles the upstream Agentation toolbar, which has its own licence, PolyForm Shield 1.0.0. Check that it fits how you use it.

match.header: Invisible to your visitors

set.header: Invisible to your visitors
set.bodytext:
Only logged-in backend users who switch it on see the toolbar, and the frontend also needs the Admin Panel option. By default it loads only in the Development context, never in production. Pages that carry the toolbar are never cached, so no visitor receives one.

Same-origin proxies let HTTPS pages reach a local agentation-mcp server. An Agentation API key is added on the server and never reaches the browser. The Content-Security-Policy is widened only for responses that carry the toolbar.

match.header: Your coding agent reads the notes over MCP

set.header: Your coding agent reads the notes over MCP
set.bodytext:
Notes go to an agentation-mcp server that your coding agent starts on your computer. With an API key, they go to the Agentation cloud instead. Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Continue and other MCP agents can read them.

The Agentation module in the System group gives you the MCP configuration, the claude mcp add command or a Cursor link. It also lists stored notes and deletes them.

assets.alternative: System > Agentation module with the MCP server configuration, a Claude Code command and status checks.
assets.description: Copy the MCP configuration and check the connection in one module.

match.header: Point at the element and write a note

set.header: Point at the element and write a note
set.bodytext: Click an element or select text, then write a note. The toolbar records the selector, the page and the computed styles, plus the page id and the user. You choose the corner it sits in, and a webhook can receive each submission with its TYPO3 context. The same toolbar runs inside backend modules. So editors can mark up the page module, record forms or your own modules.

assets.alternative: TYPO3 page module with the Agentation toolbar and a numbered note attached to a content element preview.
assets.description: The toolbar also works on backend screens such as the page module.

match.header: Feedback in words leaves the agent guessing

set.header: Feedback in words leaves the agent guessing
set.bodytext:
Clients and editors describe problems in words, like the button on the right or the heading that looks off. Your coding agent has to guess the element and the file. Screenshots in a chat lose the selector and the styles.

Agentation for TYPO3 brings the upstream Agentation toolbar into TYPO3 v14. Logged-in backend users mark up frontend pages or backend screens, and the structured context goes to the agent.

set.title: llms.txt: a site guide for AI agents
set.abstract: Every TYPO3 site and language serves an llms.txt and an agents.md from the page tree. AI agents learn what the site offers and how to use it.
set.description: Serve /llms.txt and /agents.md for every TYPO3 v14 site and language. Both come from your page tree, so AI agents find your content and interfaces.
set.og_title: llms.txt: a site guide for AI agents
set.og_description: Serve /llms.txt and /agents.md for every TYPO3 v14 site and language. Both come from your page tree, so AI agents find your content and interfaces.
set.author: Webconsulting TYPO3 Team
set.subtitle: An llms.txt and an agents.md for every TYPO3 site and language, built from the page tree

featured_image.alternative: The llms.txt of the lab site: site title, summary, a pointer to agents.md and link lists with descriptions per section.

match.header: Install llms.txt and preview the output

set.header: Install llms.txt and preview the output
set.bodytext:
composer config repositories.typo3-llms-txt vcs https://github.com/dirnbauer/typo3-llms-txt.git
composer require webconsulting/typo3-llms-txt:^1.2
vendor/bin/typo3 extension:setup --extension=llms_txt
# Preview what a site serves
vendor/bin/typo3 llmstxt:dump <site-identifier> llms.txt

Then open /llms.txt on your site. The dump command prints the same output for a review or as a CI snapshot. The code is on GitHub. Read the manual or see the feature page.

match.header: What it needs and what it stores

set.header: What it needs and what it stores
set.bodytext:
The extension needs TYPO3 v14.3 with PHP 8.4 and EXT:seo, which adds the SEO title and noindex fields. The MCP Server and the Abilities Registry are optional.

It adds no database tables and writes nothing to disk. It is free under GPL-2.0-or-later, like TYPO3.

match.header: Agents find it from any page

set.header: Agents find it from any page
set.bodytext: Every page of the site sends a Link header that points to its llms.txt, as the proposal recommends. Both files carry noindex, so search engines leave them out of their index. Two optional site settings switch a site off or add page types, and an optional site set makes them editable in the backend.

match.header: agents.md explains your machine interfaces

set.header: agents.md explains your machine interfaces
set.bodytext: The agents.md file is an operating guide for agents. It lists only the interfaces your installation really has. It names the MCP server and the Abilities Registry, with each ability's risk tier. It also names the sitemap and, with the x402 Paywall, the lane for paid content. Each entry appears only when that extension is installed.

assets.alternative: The agents.md of the lab site: MCP endpoint, abilities registry with REST and CLI access, and abilities with risk tiers.
assets.description: The agents.md lists the MCP endpoint and each ability with its risk tier.

match.header: llms.txt maps your content

set.header: llms.txt maps your content
set.bodytext:
The llms.txt follows version 2 of the llms.txt proposal. It starts with the site title and a summary, then points agents to agents.md. Each visible first-level page becomes a section, with its visible children as links, up to 25 per section. Hidden, timed-out, noindex and nav-hidden pages never appear.

Editors steer it through page properties. The root page's description becomes the summary, and each page's title and description become its link. Every language gets its own file, with translated titles and URLs.

assets.alternative: German llms.txt of the lab site with a German summary, German section titles and links to /de/ pages.
assets.description: Each language base serves its own llms.txt.

match.header: AI tools guess what your site is about

set.header: AI tools guess what your site is about
set.bodytext:
AI answers and browser agents read your site without a map. They scrape menus, miss key pages and never learn about your API. A hand-written llms.txt goes out of date with the next new page.

This extension does not hide the site from them. It serves two files for every site and language that say what the site offers and how to work with it. Both are built on each request from the page tree and the site configuration, so they stay current.

match.header: Where the files live

For integrators, each template is one page template and one folder:

match.header: Both are shadcn/ui, in every theme

set.header: Both are shadcn/ui, in every theme

match.header: Posts with contents, sharing and progress

On a post, Modern puts a table of contents next to the text. It lists the headings of the content elements, and each entry jumps to its section. Below it, readers copy the link or share the post on LinkedIn. A thin bar at the top of the window shows how far they have read.

Modern shows the newest post as a large card and the others in a grid of three. When a page ends with one or two cards, they share the last row, so no row stays half empty. The topics sit above the posts as tabs, each with its number of posts.

Classic opens with a centred masthead and shows one post after another. A date leaf sits in the margin, next to the topic, the title, a byline with the reading time, the picture and the teaser. The blog's widgets live in a sidebar on a soft panel.

match.header: Choose the look in the page properties

set.header: Choose the look in the page properties
set.bodytext:
Both templates are page templates, so editors pick them where they pick any other: in the page properties of the blog's start page, under Appearance. Choose Desiderio: Blog – Classic or Desiderio: Blog – Modern for the page and its subpages. Every post, category, tag, author and archive page below it follows.

Nothing else changes. Posts stay pages with content elements, and the EXT:blog plugins stay where they are.
